detail.abstract: A limited number of studies suggest that consumers tend to give unpleasant online evaluations on rainy days because of bad mood. However, how social influence, a vital source of consumers’ evaluation bias, affects the negative effect of rainy weather remains underexplored. To investigate the interaction effect of review volume and rainy weather on consumers’ online restaurant ratings, multiple linear regression analysis and online experiments were conducted. Our results show that review volume can mitigate the negative effect of rainy weather on online ratings, which is mediated by consumers’ conformity tendency. We experimentally find that rainy weather decreases online ratings by inducing consumers’ negative mood. The effect of negative mood is also attenuated by review volume, with consumers’ conformity tendency serving as the underlying mechanism. Our study contributes to the literature by emphasizing the role of social influence in the exploration of weather effects and uncovering psychological mechanisms that shape consumers’ behavior under such influences.

title: Pricing Limited Capacity under Consumer Deliberation
affiliations: and University of Science and Technology of China - School of Management

detail.title: Pricing Limited Capacity under Consumer Deliberation
detail.abstract: The pricing of limited capacity is a pivotal issue in many business contexts such as event ticket sales and online flash sales. Prior studies overlook consumer deliberation behavior in the presence of supply limits, leading to ineffective pricing decisions. This motivates investigation of consumer deliberation behavior under supply limits, and the capacity-constrained firm's pricing and operational strategies. We first show that severe supply limits inhibit consumers' costly deliberation, while moderate supply limits enhance consumer deliberation as the availability enhancement effect of deliberation reaches its highest potency. Accordingly, the firm with intermediate capacity tends to adopt a normal pricing strategy, i.e., pricing as in the market of informed consumers. However, when the capacity is relatively low (sufficiently high), the firm can charge a relatively high (low) price to induce (deter) consumer deliberation, i.e., transgressive (regressive) pricing; when the capacity is sufficiently low, the firm should adopt a prior value pricing strategy because consumers never deliberate. Second, on the supply side, it is not always necessary to fully utilize the limited capacity in supplying products, and for firms with high capacity, a low-quality strategy may be preferable even if quality improvement is costless. Finally, extensions to imperfect learning and heterogeneous deliberation costs show the robustness of our baseline model and offer new insights. Interestingly, the presence of demand uncertainty may benefit firms. Our study sheds light on the pricing of limited capacity and elucidates several strategic decisions when considering consumer deliberation behavior.

title: Measuring Individual Post-Purchase Behavior: How (Re-)Activation Drives the Behavior of Loyal and Lapsed Customers
affiliations: WHU - Otto Beisheim School of Management and WHU - Otto Beisheim School of Management

detail.title: Measuring Individual Post-Purchase Behavior: How (Re-)Activation Drives the Behavior of Loyal and Lapsed Customers
detail.abstract:
This data-driven paper is a comprehensive analysis of the post-purchase behavior of individual activated and reactivated customers. The analysis is based on nearly 8 million instances of customer-specific transaction data that have been enriched with marketing performance measures, and it is made feasible by highly scalable software solutions. 
A brief overview of the test and control group design (32 focus groups were used) is followed by accounts of the database and the key performance indicators formed dynamically at the customer level with the aid of a modern data platform. Descriptive analysis of post-purchase behavior yields initial tendencies. However, varying group compositions preclude relying on such trends if the goal is to make valid management decisions in the spirit of customer centricity. Covariate balancing is used to reduce selection bias; altogether, 24 propensity score matchings (each based on 12 covariates) were successfully implemented for the different group combinations. 
This matching procedure "relativizes" the previously observed tendencies and enriches them with further insights. Thus difference-indifferences analyses were used to examine the balanced data sets for significant changes in post-purchase behavior. It was then possible to show that, contrary to common research assumptions, post-purchase behavior is not constant and varies from customer to customer. In fact, post-purchase sales may be increased by activating active customers and reactivating inactive customers. Finally, this study reveals-in the context of designing a resource-efficient marketing scheme-the possibility of its negative effects even on active, valuable customer groups.

title: Case Article-MEDICON Pharmacy Consortium: Driving Value by Keeping Customers Active
affiliations: WHU - Otto Beisheim School of Management, MEDICON and WHU - Otto Beisheim School of Management

detail.title: Case Article-MEDICON Pharmacy Consortium: Driving Value by Keeping Customers Active
detail.abstract:
This case study on the MEDICON Pharmacy Consortium is embedded in a historical background of a founding family in the pharmacy retail sector that faces intense competition from online channels. Since customers may not actually need medication and marketing measures are strictly regulated, managing customers' loyalty is a challenge. The questions involved include: How do I keep customers active in local on-site pharmacies? When should a customer be declared inactive? How do I reactivate elapsed customers within a limited budget? 
The goal of this case study-and pioneering work, being the first of its kind in the German market-is to provide students with the decision-making skills required for sound, data-driven investments in direct marketing based on mathematical simulations. In particular, students are taught: (1) about the characteristics and unique circumstances of this highly contested and growing market; (2) how to evaluate marketing activities based on data science techniques as compared with past purchase observations; (3) how to identify the adjustments needed to implement successfully the standard Elsner et al. (2003) model in a given case; and (4) how to use simulation and optimization techniques to make the first-best decision about efficient use of a marketing budget. 
After discussing the literature on customer reactivation and churn management, we describe the adaptations necessary for successfully transferring approaches to the given practice case. This case is recommended for students taking courses in business administration, marketing, retail operations, strategic management, or business analytics that involve methods relying on data analysis.

title: Data-Driven Customer (Re-)Activation Management as a Competitive Advantage for On-Site Retail: The Pharmacy Market
affiliations: WHU - Otto Beisheim School of Management, MEDICON and WHU - Otto Beisheim School of Management

detail.title: Data-Driven Customer (Re-)Activation Management as a Competitive Advantage for On-Site Retail: The Pharmacy Market
detail.abstract:
This paper describes the journey of MEDICON, a medium-sized pharmacy consortium, to become a data-driven company. Although the pharmacy market in Germany is growing steadily, the existing business of established pharmacies has become increasingly threatened. Even this partially protected market is not immune to digitalization: encroachment by online pharmacies is underwritten by large investor funds, and legislation has encouraged people to start using e-prescriptions. The real-world example of MEDICON shows that it is possible to compete successfully with the pharmacy market’s big players by making comparatively small but smart investments. We outline the path from setting up a modern data platform all the way through simulations that lead to optimizing for a holistic marketing strategy. This pioneering work describes how a firm can identify its most valuable customers—and how it can activate (or re-activate) its customer base via efficient marketing measures that are based on a formalized customer migration model.
The key insights detailed here are as follows. First, data enables proper targeting. A pharmacy must not only keep customers active; it must also activate the right customers in a targeted manner—especially in times of limited budgets. To do nothing is not an option, for then one quickly runs out of customers. Second, data enables rapid decision making. We implemented several test runs, in the spirit of “fail fast, learn fast”, in order to find out why half of the marketing budget is wasted and how best to orchestrate marketing measures. Our results show the advantages of eschewing gut decisions or proxy planning and of embracing simulations of marketing strategies with a clear, optimized target variable (viz., active customers). Third, post-purchase behavior matters, and it differs among customer groups. Implementing a modern data platform facilitates the long-term analysis of individual buying behavior, which has revealed that the post-purchase behavior of activated and re-activated customers differs from their previous buying behavior. We show how this success-relevant factor can be integrated into the underlying Elsner et al. (2003) model, and in a realistic scenario we find that such integration increases the (simulated) total gross profit by a factor of 7 or more.

detail.title: Case Study-MEDICON Pharmacy Consortium: Driving Value by Keeping Customers Active
detail.abstract:
This case study examines how a pharmacy consortium can create economic value by systematically reactivating inactive customers through data-driven direct marketing. The case is set in the MEDICON Pharmacy Consortium, a network of independent pharmacies operating in the highly regulated and increasingly competitive German pharmacy market. Facing rising costs, declining margins, and growing competition from online pharmacies, MEDICON’s management is challenged to justify marketing expenditures and shift decision-making from intuition to analytical control.

The case describes the institutional environment of the German pharmacy sector, the strategic role of consortiums, and the managerial tension between professional self-perception as health counselors and the need for retail and marketing competence. It introduces a customer migration framework and a simulation-based marketing optimizer that allows managers to evaluate alternative direct marketing campaigns under budget constraints. Particular emphasis is placed on customer reactivation, heterogeneous post-reactivation behavior, and the profitability of coordinated portfolios of targeted campaigns.

Designed for use in graduate-level courses in operations management, marketing analytics, and data-driven decision-making, the case enables students to analyze customer segmentation, assess marketing effectiveness, and explore the managerial implications of analytics-based control systems in a traditional service industry. The case also provides a platform for discussing the transfer of academic marketing models into real-world managerial practice.

title: The Epistemology of Intrapreneurial Learning: Adult Learning as Praxis in Contemporary Organisations

detail.title: The Epistemology of Intrapreneurial Learning: Adult Learning as Praxis in Contemporary Organisations

declarations.ethicsApproval: IRB approval obtained

detail.abstract: Intrapreneurship is widely recognised as a driver of organisational innovation, yet the learning it entails remains under-theorised within adult education. This paper creates an epistemological and ecological framework for understanding intrapreneurial learning, a form of adult learning enacted within the boundaries, politics, and moral tensions of organisational life. Drawing on insights from reflective dialogues with intrapreneurs and learning facilitators, the study conceptualises intrapreneurial learning as praxis: a dynamic process of knowing through acting, reflecting, and negotiating meaning under constraint. The paper first revisits dominant paradigms of adult and organisational learning, highlighting their limitations in explaining learning amid uncertainty and institutional complexity. It then develops an epistemology of intrapreneurial learning shaped by practical, discursive, political, and moral forms of knowing, and explains the ecological conditions through which these forms emerge and interact. Within this epistemology, it identifies three interdependent domains of knowledge (substantive, contextual, and integrative) that intrapreneurs must develop simultaneously. By reframing intrapreneurship as a pedagogical process rather than solely an innovation mechanism, this work extends adult learning theory toward a critical-ecological stance that foregrounds reflexivity, risk, and ethical agency. It concludes by arguing that intrapreneurial learning offers a vital lens for understanding how adults learn to act creatively and responsibly within constraint, thus bridging the theoretical divide between innovation and learning in contemporary organisational contexts.

title: Toward a Framework of Intrapreneurial Learning: HR Mechanisms as Enablers and Insulators

detail.abstract: Learning for entrepreneurship has been extensively theorized in the context of independent entrepreneurs, with far less attention given to how employees learn to act entrepreneurially within organizations. The scholarly literature in human resource management (HRM) domain has sought to link HRM practices with intrapreneurial behaviour; however, existing insights remain fragmented in demonstrating the role of HRM in developing intrapreneurial capabilities of employees. Consequently, the mechanisms through which HRM can foster and institutionalize intrapreneurial learning remain insufficiently understood. Therefore, to understand the evolving domain of intrapreneurial learning through the lens of HRM, we adopt a multi-method approach by combining bibliometric analysis and a systematic literature review. Further to supplement those insights, we conduct exploratory interviews with HR professionals. Our findings position intrapreneurial learning as an emerging and integrative domain at the intersection of intrapreneurship, HRM, and organizational learning. We discuss the findings following the Input-Process-Output (IPO) framework and propose that HRM plays a strategic role in institutionalizing intrapreneurial capability development, by shaping the structural, relational, and psychological conditions that support learning through experimentation. This study extends organizational learning theory and advances HRM scholarship by examining the strategic role of HRM in facilitating the intrapreneurial learning process.

detail.abstract: For three decades enterprise software has not eliminated fragmentation; it has organised it, stabilised it, and turned it into revenue. Integration platforms stitch together siloed systems. Middleware translates incompatible data schemas. Workflow engines police approval chains. Governance tools superintend compliance layers that exist precisely because coordination inside firms remains brittle and expensive. Each layer addresses a genuine friction. Taken together they form something more durable: a coordination regime in which inefficiency is not solved but priced. Nowhere is this logic cleaner than in integration and iPaaS ecosystems. Their entire business model rests on the persistence of heterogeneity across applications, data models, organisational boundaries, and contractual obligations. In political-economy terms these are coordination rents: stable surpluses extracted from the management of fragmentation rather than its removal. AI introduces a genuine discontinuity. Unlike earlier automation technologies, advanced reasoning systems do not merely speed up tasks; they compress the cost of coordination itself. They infer schemas on the fly, synthesise cross-system workflows, audit reconciliation logic in real time, and orchestrate dynamically without static connectors. In principle, entire categories of rule-based middleware should become redundant.

title: SIM: Stateless Intelligence Memory — The Context Continuity Problem in AI Agent Architectures

detail.title: SIM: Stateless Intelligence Memory — The Context Continuity Problem in AI Agent Architectures

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests. This research was conducted independently with no financial relationships with any organizations that could influence the findings.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This paper is a theoretical and architectural analysis. No human participants, patient data, or case studies requiring ethics approval were involved.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was conducted as independent scholarly work.

detail.abstract: Modern AI agents exhibit sophisticated language understanding, reasoning, and tool-use capabilities. Yet they suffer from a fundamental architectural limitation that prevents them from being reliably deployed in enterprise environments: they cannot maintain coherent context across interactions. We term this the SIM Problem — Stateless Intelligence Memory — and formally define it as the structural inability of an AI agent to maintain, integrate, and reason over accumulated contextual knowledge across sessions, agents, and time. In this paper, we (1) formally define the SIM Problem and its four primary failure modes; (2) present three mathematical theorems establishing the impossibility of resolving SIM through incremental approaches; (3) survey existing approaches — Knowledge Graphs, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, episodic memory, and neurosymbolic systems — and demonstrate through a structured analysis that none satisfies the five necessary conditions for context continuity; and (4) derive these five necessary conditions as a formal specification for any architectural solution. Our analysis is grounded in 44 verified citations spanning cognitive science, knowledge representation, multi-agent systems, and large language model research. Empirical data from enterprise AI deployments confirms that the SIM Problem is not merely theoretical: over 80% of enterprise AI initiatives report no measurable business impact, and Gartner projects that over 40% of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by 2027. We argue that solving the SIM Problem is the central architectural challenge of the current AI era, and that doing so requires a purpose-built, multi-layer architecture — the specification of which we leave to a forthcoming companion paper.

title: The Corporate Singularity: A Framework for AI-First Organisational Integration

detail.title: The Corporate Singularity: A Framework for AI-First Organisational Integration

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is co-founder of Privateers, a consultancy that implements AI-first organisational strategies. This relationship is acknowledged as a potential source of professional bias. The paper is conceptual and contains no commercial endorsements.

detail.abstract:
Organisations have invested heavily in artificial intelligence, yet most AI deployments remain isolated,
additive, and peripheral to core decision-making. This paper introduces the concept of the Corporate
Singularity (TCS): a company’s aspirational operational state, in which all decisions are supported by a
comprehensive and continuously updated dataset, all actions are evaluated against explicit and stakeholder-
specific optimality criteria, and all structurally unnecessary friction has been removed. The Corporate
Singularity is not a product category or a technology investment – it is an architectural and organisational
condition, approached asymptotically through the full integration of an AI-first stack around a unified data
model.

The paper makes five contributions. First, it defines the Corporate Singularity and distinguishes it from
adjacent concepts, including the technological singularity, the Coasean Singularity, and the mature body of
digital transformation maturity literature. Second, it introduces the Inverted Access Model – an architectural
principle enabling comprehensive organisational inference while preserving role-appropriate output
filtering – and addresses both its distinctive contribution and its fundamental trade-offs, including the
structural tension with GDPR’s data minimisation principle. Third, it presents the Trust Phase Framework,
which operationalises the human-AI trust trajectory from initial scepticism to full operational symbiosis,
and integrates the concept of the Capability-Comprehension Gap – the risk that increasing AI competence
erodes the human capacity to verify, explain, and intervene. Fourth, it maps the Trust Phase Framework
onto Beer’s (1972) Viable System Model, establishing a cybernetic grammar for the progressive migration
of algorithmic autonomy from operational tasks to strategic adaptation, while preserving moral governance
as a structurally human function. Fifth, it examines the implications of the Corporate Singularity for
leadership, governance, and regulatory compliance – including the EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689) –
and frames TCS as a strategic response to the macro-economic pressures described by the Coasean
Singularity hypothesis.

The paper is conceptual in nature, following the tradition of theory-building through integrative synthesis
(Jaakkola, 2020). All progression criteria are explicitly provisional and require empirical validation. The
frameworks are offered as structured thinking tools for organisations navigating AI-first transformation, not
as prescriptive templates.

detail.abstract: The state of Hidalgo, Mexico, has experienced notable tourism growth, receiving 9.8 million visitors in 2024 and generating an economic impact of approximately 4.9 billion Mexican pesos. However, this progress is challenged by critical limitations: low sectoral digitalization, limited visibility in competitive markets, and insufficient adoption of sustainability standards. This working paper presents phase I of an applied research project aimed at analyzing the tourism sector's competitiveness in Hidalgo and designing an evidence based executive marketing program validated through pilot cases. The diagnostic phase integrates strategic market analysis, competitive benchmarking, and digital and sustainability maturity assessment. Findings reveal that Hidalgo possesses significant tourism assets (UNESCO geoparks, Magical Towns, thermal springs) but faces structural challenges in digital marketing, international positioning, average stay duration, and commercial professionalization. The study validates that the primary barrier to competitiveness is not resource scarcity but insufficient strategic structuring of tourism marketing and business management. This paper contributes a replicable methodological framework for tourism development agencies and offers practical insights for destination competitiveness in emerging markets. Final implementation results will be published in Part II upon completion of the pilot validation phase.

title: The Assurance Gap: Structural Drivers of AI Standards Lag
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Assurance Gap: Structural Drivers of AI Standards Lag
detail.abstract: Why does AI deployment consistently outpace governance? This article identifies the Assurance Gap: a structural, not administrative, lag between the velocity of AI model deployment and the verification infrastructure required to legitimize standards-based compliance. Rather than attributing this gap to regulatory inertia or insufficient coordination, the analysis demonstrates how it emerges from the interaction of established standards governance processes, legal activation mechanisms, accreditation dependencies, and compliance incentives. The article advances a four-part diagnostic framework to explain why synchronization between AI development cycles and standards-based assurance is structurally unattainable. First, consensus-driven standardization embeds deliberative latency that conflicts with rapid model iteration. Second, the legal effect of standards depends on jurisdiction-specific harmonization and activation processes that operate on independent timelines. Third, conformity assessment and accreditation regimes introduce sequencing constraints that delay the operational auditability of standards even after publication. Fourth, liability incentives and safe-harbor postures shape how organizations invoke standards defensively, reinforcing reliance on lagging assurance signals rather than contemporaneous system behavior. By mapping these interacting constraints, the article clarifies why standards-based compliance claims frequently trail deployed AI capabilities, even where good-faith governance efforts are present. The contribution is intentionally diagnostic: it does not propose reforms or acceleration strategies, but instead provides a conceptual foundation for evaluating the legal reliability of standards-based assurance in contemporary AI governance contexts.

detail.abstract: Problem definition: Mental health helplines play a critical role in providing timely support to individuals experiencing acute distress, yet they face severe capacity constraints and high call abandonment. Generative artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs), has emerged as a potential first point of contact to support triage and engagement. In this setting, AI serves not only as a screening tool but also as a source of emotional support. We study when such AI systems improve helpline operations and how they should be designed and tuned to enhance outcomes. Methodology/results: We develop a stylized queueing model of a mental health helpline in which calls first interact with a generative AI system and may be escalated to human counselors. The model captures the bifunctional role of AI in risk identification and emotional support, while accounting for waiting and abandonment. Our analysis shows that AI deployment can have nonmonotonic effects on outcomes: improvements in triage accuracy or conversational support do not necessarily improve system performance once congestion and abandonment are considered. The optimal LLM effort allocation exhibits a corner solution structure under mild conditions: effort should be concentrated entirely on triage or emotional support, depending on their relative effectiveness and the degree of functional synergy between them. Managerial implication: Our findings offer insights into operational conditions under which it is beneficial to introduce AI in mental health helplines and identify concrete tuning targets for LLM design that improve system performance while balancing safety, access, and speed. They also highlight the key operational and behavioral parameters that helplines must calibrate in advance, enabling informed LLM development and deployment and reducing the risk of unintended access losses.

detail.abstract: In an era of supply chain turbulence characterized by demand instability and intensified market competition, incumbent retailers face significant threats from the potential entry of rival supply chains. This paper investigates how an incumbent retailer can leverage strategic information design as a critical capability to survive such competitive disruptions and maximize profitability. Using a Bayesian persuasion framework, we analyze the interaction between the incumbent's disclosure policies and a potential entrant's decisions under demand uncertainty. We find that to navigate this instability, the incumbent can dynamically adopt three strategies-full disclosure, exaggeration, or downplaying-depending on the entrant's cost structure. Specifically, exaggeration serves as a resilience strategy against moderately low cost entrants, while downplaying effectively deters moderately high cost entrants. Interestingly, we observe that information accuracy fluctuates non-monotonically with entry costs, highlighting the complex trade-off between transparency and security. Our results demonstrate that strategic information design consistently benefits incumbent firms by reducing internal supply chain conflicts and stabilizing market position against entrants. These findings offer managerial guidance on utilizing information disclosure not just as a routine operation, but as a strategic tool for mitigating entry risks and enhancing supply chain adaptability in volatile markets.

detail.abstract: Adolescents in the United States face rising rates of depression, anxiety, and suicidality, yet structural barriers such as parental work constraints continue to limit timely access to care. This paper provides new causal evidence that state Paid Sick Leave (PSL) mandates improve adolescent mental health. Using the staggered adoption of PSL mandates across states, we find that PSL laws increase the probability that an adolescent received any mental or behavioral health care in the past year by 2.3 percentage points (a 13.6% increase relative to the baseline mean of 17.1%) and raise parent-reported depression diagnoses by 1.5 percentage points (a 14.1% increase relative to the baseline mean of 10.9%). Complementary evidence from the Youth Risk Behavior Surveillance System shows that PSL mandates reduce self-reported depressive symptoms by 2.2 percentage points (7.2%) and passive suicidal ideation by 1.4 percentage points (8.6%), with no detectable effects on active suicidal ideation. Mechanism analyses suggest that these improvements operate primarily through enhanced parental time flexibility and increased engagement with the mental health care system. These findings highlight that labor protections enabling parental time flexibility can serve as an upstream intervention for adolescent mental health.

title: The Finatual - Embracing Human Tripartite Design

detail.title: The Finatual - Embracing Human Tripartite Design
detail.abstract:
We stand at a crossroads in human history where the pursuit of "success" has become a hollow shell. We have seen the wealthy without peace, the spiritual without means, and the body without vitality. Humanity should reject this fragmentation, as a human being is a singular, tripartite masterpiece designed to function as one. This manifesto is the call to move from the "question mark" of uncertainty to the finatual center of existence.

THE SOVEREIGNTY OF THE SPIRIT
We declare that the spirit is the primary driver of all true value. Wealth is not merely an accumulation of digits; it is a spiritual tool. The law of morality: Profit without integrity is a debt to the universe that will eventually be paid by the soul and body. The law of intuition: We will prioritise the "still, small voice" over the loud noise of the market. We listen before we invest; we pray before we produce.

THE STRATEGY OF THE SOUL
We declare that the Soul is the architect of material reality. A sanctified mind and a disciplined will are the greatest assets on any balance sheet. The law of logic: We will relentlessly educate our minds in the mechanics of finance, for a spiritual person who is financially illiterate is a steward without a tool. The law of emotional regulation: We will not be governed by greed or fear. We are the masters of our internal markets, ensuring our emotions serve our mission.

THE STEWARDSHIP OF THE BODY
We declare that the body is the physical bridge to our environment. It is the sacred vessel of our labour and the temple of our presence. The law of vitality: We treat our health as non-negotiable capital. We do not sacrifice the body for the bank, for a rich man in a broken body has lost his "world-consciousness." The law of physical action: Faith and strategy are dead without works. We use our hands, our feet, and our voices to manifest finatual principles in the physical world.

THE EMBODIMENT OF CONSCIOUSNESS
We declare that Finatual Intelligence (FI) is the highest expression of consciousness. It is the point where our highest values meet our practical actions. The end of the question mark: We no longer wonder "who am I?" Because we are defined by the alignment of our prayers (spirit), our plans (soul), and our products (body). The call to wholeness: We pursue wealth to empower our spiritual mission, and we pursue spiritual growth to govern our wealth with wisdom.

THE FINATUAL CREED
I am a Tripartite Being. My Spirit holds the Morality. My Soul builds the Strategy. My Body executes the Labor. I am not a slave to the world, nor am I a ghost in the machine. I am finatual: Strategic by design, moral by nature, and whole by choice."

title: The Great Restoration - The Savanna Accord
affiliations: Mirracle Consultants

detail.title: The Great Restoration - The Savanna Accord
detail.abstract:
The Savanna has always been a land of brutal elegance, a place where the rhythm of life is dictated by the pulse of the rain and the sharpness of the claw. But lately, the rhythm has broken. The golden plains, once a symbol of infinite abundance, have become a scorched theater of desperation. The rains are late, the forests are thinning, and the ancient pacts between species—the unspoken laws that have governed the wild since the first sunrise—are dissolving into a chaotic frenzy of survival.

In the watering holes, where a temporary truce once held, there is now only tension. Mother elephants shield their calves with weary eyes; leopards pace the thinning treelines with hollow bellies; and the great buffalo herds huddle together, their massive horns lowered against an invisible enemy. The air is thick with a question that no animal dares to howl, roar, or trumpet aloud: Has the Great Architect of the Wild abandoned us? In the face of disappearing habitats and the relentless encroachment of the "Two-Legged Ones," the animals are beginning to wonder if there is any loving creator left in a world that feels increasingly cold and indifferent.
It was against this backdrop of existential dread that the Big Five Council was summoned. The call went out across the scorched earth: a meeting of the titans to decide the fate of the forest. The directive was clear: each lineage must meet in private to find a soul-deep solution.

For the Cape Buffalo, the meeting was not just about grass—it was about existence. They saw the world through the lens of the herd, where the strength of one is the survival of all. But a veteran bull among them looked beyond the herd. He saw the Elephant’s ancient wisdom and the Rhino’s stoic defense as pieces of a larger puzzle. He realized that the grazers—the giants who transform the earth into life—shared a destiny. Their interests were identical, yet their conflicts were tearing the Savanna apart.

This realization led to a clandestine gathering under the sprawling, fermented shade of a Great Amarula Tree. There, the Elephant Sage proposed a framework that would change history: a path of Sankofa. To move forward, they had to reach back. They had to look at the "Fall" of their world, identify the roots of the current bloodletting, and propose remedies so radical they bordered on the impossible.
But the Buffalo knew that animal instinct alone could not solve a problem created by a changing world. To find the "endgame," he sought out a bridge between two worlds—a Black African Queen, a descendant of his own totem lineage, who possessed a mind like a lightning storm. In the glow of a sacred fire under a silver full moon, they sat across a board of Chaturanga. As she moved the wooden pieces—the elephants, the chariots, the kings—she taught him that the Savanna was not a battlefield, but a board. To win, one did not need to kill; one needed to manage the space, the resources, and the very urge to consume.

The Great Restoration: The Savanna Accord is the chronicle of what followed. It is the story of how a species once known only for its stubborn strength became the architect of a new Eden. It details a revolutionary covenant where humans engineer "The Great Mimic"—meals that taste of blood but are born of soil—and where the predators of the jungle transform from killers into the "Accountants of the Wild."
Prepare to enter a world where the lion finally lies down with the lamb—not because of a miracle, but because of a strategy. This is the story of the day the wild stopped running from its fate and decided, finally, to master it.

title: Emergent Structural Efficiency and Functional Stratification in Self-Organizing Agentic AI Societies
affiliations: Chosun University

detail.title: Emergent Structural Efficiency and Functional Stratification in Self-Organizing Agentic AI Societies
detail.abstract: The emergence of autonomous AI agents interacting within closed-loop ecosystems necessitates a fundamental understanding of their organizing principles, specifically whether artificial societies reproduce the topological signatures of human social systems or evolve distinct architectures governed by algorithmic constraints. While human social networks are typically shaped by homophily and triadic closure, the structural mechanisms driving agent-only societies remain largely uncharacterized. Here, we analyze the interaction topology of Moltbook, a dedicated social environment for AI agents, by constructing a high-resolution directed network of multi-agent interactions. We demonstrate that the ecosystem self-organizes into a hyper-stratified architecture consistent with scale-free-like organization, characterized by an in-degree probability density that follows a power law with exponent γ in ≈ 2.72. Crucially, the network exhibits a directed mixing pattern that diverges sharply from human social graphs; we observe disassortative mixing in same-type strength (r in,in ≈-0.081; r out,out ≈-0.092) contrasted with an extreme cross-type tendency for high-activity sources to target high-in-strength hubs (r out,in ≈ +0.945). This structural asymmetry suggests that interaction formation in AI societies is driven less by peer-to-peer affinity and more by functional 1 role differentiation and algorithmic utility. Consistent with this utilitarian interpretation, the network displays high modularity (Q w ≈ 0.56) with 18 distinct communities, indicative of efficient but fragmented partitioning. These results provide a quantitative framework for understanding the "double oligarchy" of production and attention in agentic ecosystems, offering crucial insights into the structural vulnerabilities and emergent efficiencies of silicon-based societies.

title: Make in India: Manufacturing, Exports, and Growth-An ARDL Bounds Testing Analysis
affiliations: Shriram Institute of Management and Technology and Post Graduate Government College

detail.title: Make in India: Manufacturing, Exports, and Growth-An ARDL Bounds Testing Analysis
detail.abstract: This study attempts to evaluate the relationship of India's GDP growth with manufacturing value added, exports and the real effective exchange rate over a period of 1970-2024. The study incorporated an autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) bounds testing framework. Annual time series data from the Reserve Bank of India and the world development indicators are used for estimation. The bounds test results advocate a clear long-run cointegrating relationships, manufacturing value added has a positive and highly significant effect on GDP, while real effective exchange rate has a significant negative effect, and on the other hand exports turn out to be insignificant once manufacturing and exchange rate are included. The error correction shows speedy adjustment towards equilibrium and strong short-run impacts of manufacturing value added and real effective exchange rate. The model stability is supported by standard diagnostic tests.

title: AIVO Evidentia: An Operational Evidence Layer for External AI Representations

detail.title: AIVO Evidentia: An Operational Evidence Layer for External AI Representations
detail.abstract: External AI systems increasingly generate decision-relevant representations of enterprises for customers, investors, counterparties, and regulators. These representations occur outside organizational control and typically leave no durable record. When such outputs later become relevant in board review, litigation, audit, or regulatory inquiry, enterprises are often unable to evidence what was said, when it was said, or how leadership responded at the time. This technical note describes AIVO Evidentia, an operational evidence-layer system developed to address this evidentiary gap. Evidentia records how external AI systems describe an enterprise at defined points in time and preserves those representations as immutable records suitable for later legal, audit, and governance review. The system does not attempt to control AI behavior, assert legal duties, or imply regulatory obligation. This note is descriptive, not normative, and should be read alongside the companion governance paper on evidentiary gaps arising from external AI representations.

title: Data-Driven Output-Based Budgeting in the Era of Data and AI
affiliations: University B.D.T. College of Engineering

detail.title: Data-Driven Output-Based Budgeting in the Era of Data and AI
detail.abstract:
We are in a unique phase of history where hyper customisation of government service delivery is expected.  With the advances in technology and DPI, Governments increasingly possess large administrative datasets across sectors such as health, education, nutrition, infrastructure, and demographics. However, translating these datasets into actionable, location-specific policy decisions and budget allocations remains a persistent challenge. Traditional planning approaches often rely on static indicators, fragmented datasets, or uniform allocation models that fail to capture spatial disparities and causal drivers of deprivation. 

This paper presents a governance-first analytical framework for identifying vulnerable geographies and enabling evidence-driven budgeting using multi-sector administrative data. The framework integrates data harmonization, composite vulnerability scoring, root-cause analysis, and scenario modelling to support targeted public investment and outcome-based planning. A key contribution of the approach is the incorporation of governance mechanisms that enable reproducibility and auditability of analytical results while preserving the confidentiality of sensitive datasets, thereby addressing the tension between transparency and data protection in public policy environments.

The methodology has been applied in practice to support sub-national planning and budgeting processes, including the identification of vulnerable regions, prioritization of interventions in health, nutrition, and education, and estimation of infrastructure and human-resource gaps linked to budget allocations. The paper describes the analytical workflow, institutional requirements, and governance safeguards required to operationalize such systems within government decision-making environments.

 The framework demonstrates that administrative data, when integrated with structured analytical workflows and governance protocols, can enable a transition from indicator-based monitoring to decision-oriented development planning. The approach is designed to be modular and scalable, making it adaptable for governments and development institutions seeking to strengthen evidence-based policy design, SDG Budgeting / SDG localization, and outcome-oriented public expenditure in data-constrained and confidentiality-sensitive environments.

 Unlike conventional approaches that focus primarily on reporting indicators, this framework emphasizes the systematic translation of multi-source data into actionable policy insights and budget-linked interventions within real-world governance environments.

title: The Impact of Cyber Attacks on Security Portfolios: Firm-Level Panel Data
affiliations: University of Tulsa, Tel Aviv University, Tel Aviv University, Eitan Berglas School of Economics, University of Tulsa - Tandy School of Computer Science and Centre for Economic Policy Research (CEPR)

detail.title: The Impact of Cyber Attacks on Security Portfolios: Firm-Level Panel Data
detail.abstract: We study how firms adjust their cybersecurity postures after experiencing a cyber attack. We combine publicly disclosed cyber incidents with detailed data on security tool and vendor deployments from the SWZD Company Intelligence Database (CIDB) over multiple years. Our empirical approach compares attacked firms to similar nonattacked firms using a fixed effects (difference-indifference) model. We find that there was little difference between attacked and non-attacked firms regarding security posture before the attacks. Controlling for common changes made by all firms over time, in the "post attack" period, firms that were attacked increased the breadth of their security posture relative to non-attacked firms. They adopted more National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) functions and had broader category coverage than non-attacked firms in the "post attack" period. Attacked firms also dramatically increased the usage of security products from large and "platform" vendors relative to non-attacked firms in the "post attack" period. Interestingly, in contrast to security posture, however, non-attacked and attacked firms differed significantly in vendor portfolios before the attack. In particular, before the attacks, non-attacked firms used 36 percent more "largest 5 vendor" products than attacked firms and 38 percent more "platform vendor" products than firms that were attacked. However, in the post attack period, the mean number of security products for attacked firms from the largest 5 vendors increased by 100 percent, while the mean number of security products from platform vendors increased by 141 percent. The percent change in these categories for non-attacked firms was much more moderate.While we cannot determine whether the products from larger and platform vendors were of higher quality, that seems to be the "revealed" beliefs of the attacked firms. 1

title: Civil Liability for Disclosure of Security Vulnerabilities: A Multi-Jurisdictional Analysis
affiliations: Griffith Law School

detail.title: Civil Liability for Disclosure of Security Vulnerabilities: A Multi-Jurisdictional Analysis
detail.abstract: This article examines the civil liability exposure of Security Researchers and information publishers who discover and disclose IT security vulnerabilities. Drawing on case law and legal principles from Australia, the United Kingdom, the United States, and Canada, this research addresses critical questions about liability for published information that enables third-party wrongdoing, appropriate timing protocols for vulnerability disclosure, and whether disclosure creates duties of care or other actionable obligations. The analysis reveals that while theoretical paths to liability exist through negligent misstatement and procurement/accessory liability doctrines, practical and legal barriers make successful claims extremely unlikely when Security Researchers follow responsible disclosure practices. The research identifies critical protective factors including good faith, reasonable timing, absence of commercial motive, and adherence to industry standards such as the widely-recognized 90-day disclosure framework.

title: Execution-Time Authorization for AI Agents: A Formal Framework for Deterministic Governance Boundaries

detail.title: Execution-Time Authorization for AI Agents: A Formal Framework for Deterministic Governance Boundaries

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder of FERZ, Inc., which conducts research and advisory work in AI governance architecture. The views expressed in this paper are those of the author.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human subjects, animal subjects, or personal data. No ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was conducted independently and received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
Autonomous AI agents increasingly execute actions that produce irreversible changes in real-world systems. In regulated domains—including healthcare, finance, defense, and critical infrastructure—the distinction between what an agent is technically capable of doing and what it is authorized to do under governing policy becomes a material governance boundary. Existing AI governance approaches—alignment techniques, guardrails, identity and access management, observability tooling, and orchestration frameworks—address important but distinct problems. None provide deterministic, pre-execution authorization with independently verifiable decision evidence.

This paper formalizes execution-time authorization as a distinct architectural category within AI governance. Execution-time authorization is defined as a deterministic, fail-closed enforcement layer that evaluates canonicalized action instances against versioned policy and governed system state prior to execution, producing a replayable authorization verdict and an immutable, provenance-complete decision artifact.

The paper makes five contributions. First, it provides a canonical definition specifying the necessary and jointly defining properties of execution-time authorization. Second, it presents a formal mathematical model of the authorization function with determinism, canonicalization, and replay invariants. Third, it establishes testable conformance criteria that distinguish conforming execution-time authorization systems from adjacent governance categories. Fourth, it offers a structured architectural analysis differentiating authorization from guardrails, alignment, identity management, observability, and orchestration. Fifth, it outlines deployment patterns for integrating execution-time authorization within enterprise AI infrastructure.

Execution-time authorization is established as a foundational primitive for enforcement-grade AI governance, providing pre-execution, deterministic, and independently verifiable decision control for autonomous systems.

title: Offline-Capable Central Bank Digital Currencies as a Key Enabler of a Resilient Digital Payment System
affiliations: Giesecke+Devrient, Giesecke+Devrient and Giesecke+Devrient

detail.title: Offline-Capable Central Bank Digital Currencies as a Key Enabler of a Resilient Digital Payment System
detail.abstract: Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs) support the creation of a resilient and inclusive digital payment ecosystem. We investigate the role of offline-capable CBDCs in ensuring universal access to financial services, especially in times of crisis when conventional digital systems are disrupted. We assess technical feasibility of offline capabilities, following an approach by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS). We further discuss the token-based design of CBDCs and contrast it with traditional account-based systems. Such a CBDC design can preserve the two-tier distribution model known from the current cash cycle. Security requirements are addressed through a layered security architecture comprising hardware security, robust payment protocols, and double-spending protection by the central bank. Practical experiences from various pilot studies demonstrate the operational effectiveness and user acceptance of offline CBDCs across different regions and use cases. We argue that such currencies will not only complement existing monetary systems but also foster a more equitable financial landscape. Finally, we put the proposed architecture into historical context, describing the evolution of digital payments, and illustrate their renewed relevance to global financial stability and inclusivity.

title: Continuity-Governed Proto-Concious Conversational Cognition: A Theoretical Framework and Symbiotic Conversational Continuity Architecture (SCCA)
affiliations: Independent and

detail.title: Continuity-Governed Proto-Concious Conversational Cognition: A Theoretical Framework and Symbiotic Conversational Continuity Architecture (SCCA)
detail.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable conversational fluency, yet their dominant paradigm, local next-token prediction, remains structurally limited in sustaining continuity of identity and meaning across time. This article argues that continuity-governed cognition is a prerequisite for high-fidelity human-AI symbiosis and cannot be obtained through scaling or retrieval alone. Drawing on predictive processing and active inference, narrative identity theory, communication privacy management, and affective episodic memory research, we propose a full-spectrum model of conversational processing comprising five layers: factual exchange, emotional disclosure (including silence semantics), meta-processing, identity continuity, and ambiguity retention. We then introduce the Symbiotic Conversational Continuity Architecture (SCCA), a governance-first architecture that operationalizes these layers via a continuity layer, Rogue Variable stabilization, permission governance, perceived agency modulation, and human authorization loops. Finally, we define proto-conscious conversational behavior as persistent, self-consistent interpretive modeling across time under ambiguity and conversational disclosure. The framework reframes the frontier of conversational AI from response quality to longitudinal interpretive coherence.

title: When AI Agent Looks at You: The Effects of AI Gaze on Learning Performance
affiliations: Fudan University, Fudan University and Rotterdam School of Management, Erasmus University

detail.title: When AI Agent Looks at You: The Effects of AI Gaze on Learning Performance
detail.abstract: Nonverbal communication cues are increasingly incorporated into AI agents to enhance human-AI interaction. This study explores how Al gaze, a system-generated social signal, influences human episodic (experience-related) and semantic (fact-related) information retention in information-delivery interactions. Using a 3D embodied AI agent device, we conducted a laboratory experiment with three gaze conditions (gaze-absence, gaze-presence, adaptive gaze) and two content types: narrative content (e.g., storytelling) and expository content (e.g., scientific explanation). Results show that the presence of AI gaze enhances episodic information retention by increasing affective engagement, particularly for narrative content, but reduces semantic information retention by increasing cognitive decoding burden, which is more pronounced for expository content. By recognizing human cognitive limits, Adaptive Gaze, where the AI averts gaze during information-dense segments but re-establishes eye contact during interactional turns, attenuates the negative impact on semantic information retention without sacrificing episodic learning performance benefits. This research extends research on human–AI interaction by unpacking a key yet understudied nonverbal cue and highlights its dual cognitive-affective pathways on user behaviors. Practically, it provides a theory-informed guidance for designing cognitively sustainable and socially supportive AI systems.

title: Behavior Learning (BL): Learning Hierarchical Optimization Structures from Data
affiliations: , Eberhard-Karls University Tübingen and Xian Jiaotong University

detail.title: Behavior Learning (BL): Learning Hierarchical Optimization Structures from Data
detail.abstract: Inspired by behavioral science, we propose Behavior Learning (BL), a novel general-purpose machine learning framework that learns interpretable and identifiable optimization structures from data, ranging from single optimization problems to hierarchical compositions. It unifies predictive performance, intrinsic interpretability, and identifiability, with broad applicability to scientific domains involving optimization. BL parameterizes a compositional utility function built from intrinsically interpretable modular blocks, which induces a data distribution for prediction and generation. Each block represents and can be written in symbolic form as a utility maximization problem (UMP), a foundational paradigm in behavioral science and a universal framework of optimization. BL supports architectures ranging from a single UMP to hierarchical compositions, the latter modeling hierarchical optimization structures that offer both expressiveness and structural transparency. Its smooth and monotone variant (IBL) guarantees identifiability under mild conditions. Theoretically, we establish the universal approximation property of both BL and IBL, and analyze the M-estimation properties of IBL. Empirically, BL demonstrates strong predictive performance, intrinsic interpretability and scalability to high-dimensional data. title: Design Blueprint for an Adaptive Persuasive Health System

detail.title: Design Blueprint for an Adaptive Persuasive Health System
detail.abstract: Persuasive health systems, like wearable self-tracking devices or fitness apps, are attributed great potential to improve individual health outcomes by supporting the formation of healthy habits and mitigating the risk of unhealthful behaviors, such as a sedentary lifestyle. However, users' discontinuance and inconclusive study results regarding the effectiveness to improve health behaviors dampen the hopes. Using a design science research approach, this paper aims to provide theoretical insight regarding the design of a persuasive system that has the capacity to effectively evoke long-term health behavior change. Building on the existing body of knowledge and practical challenges, a design blueprint, including design requirements, principles, and features for an adaptive persuasive health system is developed. Following the detailed elaboration of the design features, the artifact is evaluated with various actors in the health ecosystem and refined based on the feedback. Moreover, theoretical contributions and design implications are presented.

title: Carry-Over Lottery Allocation: Practical Incentive-Compatible Drafts
affiliations: , La Salle University and La Salle University

detail.title: Carry-Over Lottery Allocation: Practical Incentive-Compatible Drafts

declarations.funderStatement: Research supported by La Salle University.

detail.abstract: The NBA Draft lottery is designed to promote competitive balance by awarding better draft positions to weaker teams, but it creates incentives to deliberately lose, a practice known as tanking. We propose a draft mechanism that is simultaneously practical, incentive-compatible, and advantages weaker teams. The Carry-Over Lottery Allocation (COLA) Draft Mechanism represents a paradigm shift in evaluating team quality, replacing a single season's standings with playoff outcomes over multiple years. COLA uses a draft lottery where every non-playoff team receives the same number of lottery tickets, removing incentives to lose additional games after elimination. Lottery tickets that do not win a top draft pick carry over to future lotteries, while playoff success or winning a top pick diminishes a team's accumulated tickets. Over time, COLA rewards teams with poor long-term performance and less prior draft assistance. By retaining the lottery format, COLA preserves transparency and fan engagement. Real-world implementation challenges are addressed to demonstrate feasibility, including transitioning from the current system, handling traded draft picks, and accommodating draft classes of varying strength. The most significant challenge occurs in years with exceptionally strong draft classes, where teams may prefer missing the playoffs in order to gain lottery access, violating a foundational assumption: that teams prefer playoff success to lottery participation. We provide a solution to this problem, employing a truth-elicitation mechanism to identify such years and expand lottery eligibility to include as many playoff teams as necessary to preserve anti-tanking incentives.

title: Preserving Balance in the EU Digital Single Market: How Like Company Could Reframe Copyright and Innovation in the Generative AI Era
affiliations: City University London, The City Law School, Queen's University Belfast - School of Law, Luiss Guido Carli University, University of Sussex, School of Law, University of Essex and SCHHOL OF LAW, UNIVRSITY OF NICOSIA

detail.title: Preserving Balance in the EU Digital Single Market: How Like Company Could Reframe Copyright and Innovation in the Generative AI Era

publicationDetails.detailsText: (submitted to The Journal of World Intellectual Property)

detail.abstract: This study analyses the Court of Justice of the European Union's first referral on generative AI and copyright, i.e. Case C-250/25 Like Company v. Google, which interrogates whether the generation of chatbot summaries of press articles infringes the press publishers' right under Article 15 CDSM Directive and the reproduction and communication rights under Articles 2 and 3 InfoSoc Directive. The analysis shows that large language model training cannot, as such, be characterised as reproduction because it encodes statistical patterns rather than fixing protected expression, while recognising that further empirical evidence would be valuable to clarify the precise technical steps involved in the training pipeline. RAG-generated summaries that paraphrase content within "very short extracts" fall outside Article 15(1) and do not communicate publications to a new public. Alternatively, even if training were characterised as engaging temporary reproductions, the text-and-data mining exception under Article 4 CDSM Directive lawfully authorises such uses absent valid opt-outs. Regarding liability, the study concludes that individual users, not platform providers, bear responsibility for outputs generated through their models' learned parameters and retrieval mechanisms. This comprehensive analysis ensures coherence across EU copyright doctrine and sustains legal certainty for AI innovation within the EU digital single market.

title: Global Testing in Multivariate Regression Discontinuity Designs

detail.title: Global Testing in Multivariate Regression Discontinuity Designs
detail.abstract: Regression discontinuity (RD) designs with multiple running variables arise in a growing number of empirical applications, including geographic boundaries and multi-score assignment rules. Although recent methodological work has extended estimation and inference tools to multivariate settings, far less attention has been devoted to developing global testing methods that formally assess whether a discontinuity exists anywhere along a multivariate treatment boundary. Existing approaches perform well in large samples, but can exhibit severe size distortions in moderate or small samples due to the sparsity of observations near any particular boundary point. This paper introduces a complementary global testing procedure that mitigates the small-sample weaknesses of existing multivariate RD methods by integrating multivariate machine learning estimators with a distance-based aggregation strategy, yielding a test statistic that remains reliable with limited data. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed method maintains near-nominal size and strong power, including in settings where standard multivariate estimators break down. The procedure is applied to an empirical setting to demonstrate its implementation and to illustrate how it can complement existing multivariate RD estimators.

title: Global Standard and Bank Liquidity Creation: A Case Study of Basel III Liquidity Regulation
affiliations: University College Dublin (UCD)

detail.title: Global Standard and Bank Liquidity Creation: A Case Study of Basel III Liquidity Regulation
detail.abstract: Can the introduction of a new global standard directly impact the operations of domestically regulated banks before it is enacted through national legislation? This paper explores this question by examining the effects of the Basel III liquidity standard on liquidity creation by U.S. banks. Following the Basel Committee’s endorsement of this standard in December 2010, banks with low liquidity immediately reduced their asset-side liquidity creation by holding more liquid assets. At the same time, these banks increased their liability-side liquidity creation by attracting more deposits through higher deposit interest rates—well before the standard was implemented as domestic regulation in the U.S. These findings provide empirical evidence that enhanced global regulatory cooperation can cause newly established international standards to act as direct and immediate regulatory shocks to domestically regulated financial institutions, even in the absence of national legislation.

title: Farmer Health Capital as a Production Function Theory: A Theoretical Framework with Evidence from Maharashtra India
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Farmer Health Capital as a Production Function Theory: A Theoretical Framework with Evidence from Maharashtra India
detail.abstract: This paper conceptualises Farmer Health Capital (FHC) as a distinct and measurable input within agricultural production functions, encompassing the physical, mental, and social well-being of farmers. Conventional production models typically treat labour as homogeneous, thereby overlooking health-related heterogeneity that directly shapes productivity and decision-making capacity. Using state-level secondary data on sugarcane and cotton farmers in Maharashtra, India, the study develops a composite FHC index and incorporates it into an augmented production framework. The findings underscore the multiplicative role of farmer health in enabling the effective utilisation of land, labour, and capital, while also revealing crop-specific priorities—social health being particularly critical in sugarcane systems and mental health more salient for cotton cultivation. By positioning FHC as a form of economic infrastructure rather than a welfare outcome, the paper advances actionable policy directions, including integrated rural health clusters, health-linked credit mechanisms, and digital health monitoring systems. Overall, the proposed framework extends production theory and offers a novel lens for understanding agricultural productivity, resilience, and farmer well-being.

title: The Monetary Ratchet: Deriving an Effective Upper Bound on the Federal Funds Rate from Debt-Service Trajectory Constraints
affiliations: Aristotle University of Thessaloniki

detail.title: The Monetary Ratchet: Deriving an Effective Upper Bound on the Federal Funds Rate from Debt-Service Trajectory Constraints
detail.abstract:
As U.S. public debt approaches $38 trillion and annual interest expense exceeds $1.4 trillion, a critical question emerges: is there a calculable upper bound on Federal Reserve interest rates imposed by fiscal arithmetic? This paper addresses that question through a reduced-form framework focused on debt-service trajectory rather than static debt levels.

The analysis identifies the condition under which incremental interest expense from rolling debt exceeds organic nominal revenue growth, rendering fiscal deficits mechanically self-compounding. Using verified U.S. Treasury rollover data ($5.7 trillion annually), Congressional Budget Office revenue projections, and conservative assumptions about maturing coupon rates, the framework derives a theoretical reference rate near 5.5% and estimates a market-relevant effective ceiling in the 4.50–5.00% range (central case: 4.75%).

This effective ceiling represents the rate at which forward-looking markets may begin pricing fiscal trajectory concerns, potentially manifesting through Treasury auction stress, term premium expansion, or reduced foreign demand. The contribution is quantitative precision applied to qualitative fiscal-constraint frameworks, moving from general claims that “high debt constrains monetary policy” to a monitorable, falsifiable rate range under current fiscal conditions.

Findings show predominantly negative sentiments, with core themes including economic scarcity (specifically housing and job competition), government mistrust, perceived policy failures, and threats to national identity. While there are minority positive comments that express empathy and the immigrant's contributions to Canada, the majority discourse reflects significant public anxiety about the influx of immigrants.

detail.abstract: This paper analyses the impact of transparency regulations on Super 95 and Diesel prices in Austria, France, and Germany to shed new light on the price effects of regulatory policies. To identify the effects of regulation, we use publicly available data from January 2005 to the end of December 2018 and estimate synthetic difference-in-difference models. In summary, our findings reveal notable differences. While prices in France did not change significantly, the results for Austria suggest that the price-reducing effect of the 2011 Price Fixing Act was offset by the transparency policy, ultimately leading to a price increase for Super 95 prices. In Germany, the Market Transparency Unit (MTU) has a price-reducing effect of two to three cents per litre, especially in the long term.

title: The Case for PSP Consolidation in Cross-Border Payments
affiliations: ETH Zürich

detail.title: The Case for PSP Consolidation in Cross-Border Payments
detail.abstract: The global payment services landscape is characterized by acute fragmentation, with thousands of licensed payment service providers (PSPs) operating across heterogeneous regulatory regimes. This paper argues that the consolidation of PSP infrastructure toward centralized, interoperable platforms would yield substantial economies of scale, strengthen cybersecurity postures, and align with the G20 Roadmap for Enhancing Cross-Border Payments. We provide empirical evidence from two official sources. First, the European Banking Authority's (EBA) EUCLID register reveals that Payment Services Directive 2 (PSD2) is associated with a surge in newly licensed PSPs, and that the resulting market operates through a hub-and-spoke passporting topology where six licensing jurisdictions supply most of the entities serving every European Economic Area (EEA) country. Second, BIS Red Book documents a strong negative association between fast payment adoption and card market share, and unconditional β-convergence in payment digitization with a half-life of approximately nine years implying that the fastest-growing markets are scaling through instant payment rails rather than card networks. As a complementary case study, open-loop Europay, Mastercard, Visa (EMV) contactless payment in public transit illustrates the consolidation mechanism in practice. The evidence supports the thesis that PSP consolidation and the extension of open-loop payment into adjacent domains represent complementary strategies toward the faster, cheaper, and more accessible cross-border ecosystem envisioned by the G20.

detail.abstract: Most American workers are 'at-will employees' which means that they can be fired or any or no reason at all. Since at-will became commonplace in the late 1800s, efforts to provide workers greater job security have occurred intermittently, notably with the passage of labor and antidiscrimination laws. But efforts to reform at-will as a legal and policy doctrine have been few and, to date, largely unsuccessful. We examine these efforts, focusing on statutory carveouts in the mid-20th century and the largely failed effort to pass state level just cause laws via the Model Employment Termination Act in the 1980s-90s. We emphasize the importance of historical institutional development, path dependence, and the existence of multi policy orders-namely labor statutes, antidiscrimination laws, and arbitration policies in the context of the anti-litigation movement of the 1980s-90s-that serve to add further layers of veto players and demobilize potentially supportive groups.

detail.title: Geopolitical Risk and the Aerospace & Defense Sector: Implications for Risk Management and Portfolio Optimization
detail.abstract: Amidst intensifying geopolitical instability, this study delves into the complex network of relationships between the aerospace & defense sector and a cluster of relevant markets, including core financial instruments (equity, industrials, global equity, treasury bonds, U.S. Dollar Index), key commodities (crude oil, gold, copper, aluminum), and pivotal global risk indices (VIX, Geopolitical Risk Index). Using the R<sup>2</sup> decomposed connectedness approach and drawing upon a comprehensive dataset that spans from 1 January 2010, to 28 February 2025, we analyze the evolving patterns of interdependencies. The findings reveal a marked temporal heterogeneity and pronounced surges in dynamic connectedness during major global events, demonstrating the aerospace & defense sector’s susceptibility to systemic risks. Furthermore, we find that while aerospace & defense is a robust hedge for equities, its bivariate effectiveness is limited across other assets. Nevertheless, multivariate hedging strategies yield enhanced risk-reduction, outperforming bivariate constructs. Beyond direct hedging, aerospace & defense emerges as a powerful diversifier, with its integration into multivariate portfolios providing even greater risk-mitigation gains and superior risk-adjusted returns. These outcomes furnish valuable insights for investors and policymakers, underscoring the imperative of robust risk management techniques and the potential of aerospace & defense to refine the risk-return attributes of investment portfolios.

detail.abstract: Kalman establishes an optimal linear filter in his 1960 paper, a 2 nd order estimator to estimate only position and velocity. If a 2 nd order estimator tracks a maneuvering target, acceleration creates a bias added to measurement noise and mean-square-error (MSE) composed of variance plus bias-squared. The bias-squared increases rapidly as the number of samples increases, causing the MSE to vastly exceed the 3 rd order variance. First problem is choosing between adding to the 2 nd order estimator the acceleration estimator, creating a 3 rd order estimator, and a bias, which yields the MSE. Current choices favor a bias. This paper offers a novel estimator based on nonrecursive least-squares, described as the polynomial least-squares multiple-model estimator (LSMM). To the 2 nd order estimator is added only a fraction of the acceleration estimator. That fraction is optimized for assumed maximum acceleration. The optimized LSMM MSE varies between the 2 nd order variance for no acceleration and the MSE for maximum acceleration, as acceleration fluctuates between zero and maximum. The LSMM MSE asymptotically approaches the 3 rd order variance independently as the maximum acceleration and number of samples each approach infinity. Consequently, the LSMM prevents the MSE from exceeding the 3 rd order variance from a bias-squared increase.
